mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-rising periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 60-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future earnings and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite consistent monthly PCE growth above the threshold (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month indicates supply-side weakness, which raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly lower than during normal production growth periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, it indicates a shift toward tighter policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to equities and results in negative 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically different from the pre-tightening period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of unemployment rate falling below 4% while labor force participation remains stable creates a labor market tightening that supports risk-on sentiment and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months with no significant change in PAYEMS
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no significant correlation with the labor market tightening signal (Pearson IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales (not available in the provided proxies - skip this and use alternative) -- instead: A rapid increase in housing starts (not available) -- instead: A sustained monthly rise in consumer confidence proxy (not available) -- instead: A sharp increase in GDP deflator inflation (not available) -- instead: Use HOUST as a demand proxy: A monthly surge in HOUST above 3% suggests accelerating demand for housing, which translates to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises above 3% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3% for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 exhibits a higher probability of positive 20-day forward returns compared to a tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 3.5%), regardless of other signals.
candidate_trigger: regime condition: FEDFUNDS < 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the easing regime, 20-day forward returns are not significantly more positive than in the tightening regime (log-odds ratio p > 0.05).
